races.name: Bath And Wiltshire Air Ambulance Handicap

runners_data.name: Lavender Bloom
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly whose three career runs have all come at six furlongs or on Good ground — dropping to five-and-a-half on Firm is an untested combination, and she carries 135lbs for Steph Hollinshead; if the pace is genuinely honest she is the one most likely to land a late blow, but the slow-pace scenario this race shape implies is far from ideal.|
runners_data.comment: Green on all three outings and unplaced again at this course last time, she has shown inexperience rather than absence of ability; stepping into handicap company for the first time could unlock more, though both the drop in trip and the firm ground are mild reservations.

runners_data.name: Geemann
runners_data.note: Joe Tickle's three-year-old is a true hold-up type by inclination, as a fade-prone finisher whose last five runs all ended outside the top eight on Good ground — he is shown in midfield here purely because the map cannot place all rear-division horses at the back, and his chance should be tempered accordingly; Taylor Fisher takes over for the first time.|
runners_data.comment: Sprint-bred and apparently effective at 6f, he ran far too freely and finished well down the field at Bath most recently; a stocky type with plenty still to prove in handicap company, his last five starts have yielded nothing and he is hard to recommend here.

runners_data.name: Reality Queen
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's filly has rattled through her races regularly (11-day turnaround) and her form line of 45-775 shows solid consistency without a win — as the hold-up runner with the most promising recent placings she is arguably the best of the closers, though the uncontested pace scenario does not set this race up for her.|
runners_data.comment: Her run at Newmarket last time looks a fitness-builder and she should strip sharper here; acts on fast ground and 6f suits well, though she ideally wants more ease underfoot than today offers. Yet to win in recent starts, but capable of better once sharper.

runners_data.name: Rosieisme Darling
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner with a style-fit flag, meaning she is operating outside a strictly prominent role, but in a five-runner field with no pace rival she should take the lead effortlessly; Luke Morris is adept at managing front-running rides, and her form of 364324 shows genuine consistency — the Firm ground at Bath should not inconvenience her.|
runners_data.comment: Matched her level when beaten under three lengths off a slightly higher mark last time, she has been a consistent placer in recent outings at 5/6f; versatile on ground and well weighted today, she has a solid claim here.

runners_data.name: Rogue Rebellion
runners_data.note: Ronald Harris's gelding has shown he can place (2s at Goodwood and Yarmouth) when conditions suit but has finished ninth twice recently on Good ground — a genuine hold-up horse pushed into a midfield slot by redistribution, his style-fit discount is real; Kieran O'Neill takes the ride for a trainer who has yet to strike in four attempts over the past fortnight.|
runners_data.comment: Capable of better on his day, with two placings and a win among his last six starts, but well beaten at Bath most recently with nothing to explain it; must recover from a pair of poor efforts and find his earlier level to factor here.

races.paceDynamic: Rosieisme Darling is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a five-runner field, she should coast across to the rail and set a controlled, unhurried gallop on firm ground at Bath. This is a steady, uncontested pace scenario — on a flat five-and-a-half furlong track in firm conditions, that translates to a race run at a rhythm that preserves the leader's stamina rather than burning it. The hold-up brigade — Lavender Bloom, Geemann, Reality Queen, and Rogue Rebellion — must come from behind a horse that will never be seriously tested early, meaning the closing kick needs to be both significant and timed perfectly to bridge the gap. The race shape strongly favours prominent racers and the front-runner herself, as hold-up horses face an uphill task when the pace is not genuinely strong enough to string the field out and set up a true late rush. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than can be accommodated at the rear; Geemann and Rogue Rebellion are naturally rear-division horses mapped to midfield, but Rosieisme Darling is most likely to secure the only meaningful forward berth and dictate throughout.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rosieisme Darling Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Rosieisme Darling breaks cleanly and sets a comfortable, uncontested tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: If Rosieisme Darling breaks cleanly and sets a comfortable, uncontested tempo throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Grab It
scenarios.trigger: If Rosieisme Darling goes too hard early or the pace is stronger than expected, tying herself up in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Rosieisme Darling goes too hard early or the pace is stronger than expected, tying herself up in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Rosieisme Darling weakens gradually and redistributed hold-up horses Geemann and Rogue Rebellion find themselves in a better position than their natural style suggests.
scenarios.body: If Rosieisme Darling weakens gradually and redistributed hold-up horses Geemann and Rogue Rebellion find themselves in a better position than their natural style suggests.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so pedestrian that all five runners arrive at the two-furlong pole in a cluster and the race becomes a sprint finish from close range.
scenarios.body: If the pace is so pedestrian that all five runners arrive at the two-furlong pole in a cluster and the race becomes a sprint finish from close range.

watchPoints.text: Watch Rosieisme Darling's break from the stalls — if Luke Morris gets her away cleanly with no early pressure, the race is effectively hers to lose and all hold-up runners face a significant challenge.|

Geemann's fade-in-finish flag combined with his redistribution to midfield is a double negative — if he is drifting in the market, it likely reflects that his true running position and recent form both work against him here.|

Lavender Bloom drops in distance to five-and-a-half furlongs for the first time and carries the joint-highest weight at 135lbs — monitor whether David Egan settles her quickly, as an unsettled hold-up horse on a flat track with a slow pace will find it almost impossible to produce a winning burst.|

Reality Queen's 11-day turnaround and Alistair Rawlinson's booking for Michael Appleby is worth noting — Appleby has 3 from 27 over the past 14 days, suggesting the yard is in a fair vein, and she is the most consistent of the hold-up horses if the pace does collapse.|

races.name: British EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Angel Ang
runners_data.comment: Came away decisively on debut, impressing in a 6f novice and clearly knowing his job from the outset — there should be more to come. Carries a penalty for that success but sets the standard in a field where debut form counts for much.

runners_data.name: Chasingpursuit
runners_data.comment: A 40,000 guineas Dark Angel colt who debuts in first-time blinkers; his stable is in good form and has a track record of producing debutants ready to run. His dam was unraced but his sire gives speed, and the market will be informative.

runners_data.name: Empire Rising
runners_data.comment: Took a step forward second time out when fourth at Salisbury, beaten three and a quarter lengths — there is room for further progress if he handles the switch to faster ground. His trainer is in strong form and he has the breeding for speed, though a wide draw is not ideal.

runners_data.name: Parkers Light
runners_data.comment: An Oasis Dream gelding making his debut from a wide draw — the market will be informative and his pedigree suggests speed over this sort of trip. His dam showed smart form at six furlongs, and while all to prove first time out, the breeding is encouraging.

runners_data.name: Harry's Pop
runners_data.comment: Stepped up on his debut showing when fourth at Chester last time, running freely but still finding improvement as he gained experience. He stays the trip and handles the ground, and could progress further if settling more smoothly, despite the wide draw.

runners_data.name: King Koopa
runners_data.comment: Showed a promising debut when fourth at Wolverhampton, looking like he knew what was required, and he has speed in his pedigree over this sort of trip. His trainer is out of form of late, though he acts on this going and should come on for the experience.

runners_data.name: Pj's Corner
runners_data.comment: Made some progress second time out at Ripon when beaten six and a half lengths, gaining a little from his debut experience. However, he needs a significant step forward here and his pedigree points to longer trips in time, making him hard to fancy over today's distance.

runners_data.name: Theheatison
runners_data.comment: Gained from the debut experience when fifth at Salisbury last time, beaten three and a quarter lengths, and he handles this distance and going. He should do better as he matures and may eventually prove best over a longer trip, but remains a threat on current form.

runners_data.name: Soldier's Echo
runners_data.comment: A newcomer by sprinter Soldier's Call for a yard that turns out debutants ready to run. Full-sister to the smart miler Soldier's Gold and out of the top-flight miler Copperbeech, so this longer trip should play to her pedigree.

runners_data.name: Texas Crown
runners_data.comment: Showed inexperience when well beaten on his only start at Salisbury, never getting competitive. His pedigree is all about speed which suits the trip, but he needs to translate that potential onto the track and faces a stern test in a race of this depth.

runners_data.name: Dissenter
runners_data.comment: A 14,000 guineas Kodi Bear filly making her debut; her dam showed useful ability at seven furlongs as a two-year-old and nearly landed a race on her second start. An unlikely prospect to prevail on debut but the breeding gives some grounds for market interest.

runners_data.name: Velma Dinkley
runners_data.comment: Showed inexperience when beaten nine lengths on debut at Windsor, but there were signs she was still learning. Her breeding suggests she will get a mile in time, and a six-week break may have helped — though she likely needs more outings to be seen at her best.

races.name: Hot Air Balloon Company Handicap

runners_data.name: Neptune Legend
runners_data.note: Sharp and in-form seven-year-old with back-to-back wins at Goodwood over 6f on good ground; David Egan takes over and the two-day turnaround after a quick comeback win is the key angle — hold-up style but capable of travelling prominently enough to find cover.|
runners_data.comment: Has course form and handles this distance and firm ground well, having taken a win at Bath three starts ago. He is back on the same mark as his fifth last time and keeps a manageable rating, making him a genuine danger despite returning on a tight schedule.

runners_data.name: Ten Club
runners_data.note: Returned after 148 days off the mark over 7f at Southwell, but has been consistently trailing the field over 7f on soft/standard surfaces since; the drop to 5½f on firm at Bath looks a significant ask and the long absence before that recent run raises fitness questions.|
runners_data.comment: Returning after a lengthy absence of almost five months, during which his form had deteriorated well before the break — he was beaten without obvious excuse in his final start. Now back below his last winning mark, he needs to recapture earlier ability to feature here.

runners_data.name: Hidden Verse
runners_data.note: Form shows a second at Goodwood over 6f on good and solid 5th/5th on fast and good ground, giving genuine similar-going relevance; true hold-up horse whose natural style is compromised by having nowhere to go at the rear in this field, making clean passage essential for the claim to be realised.|
runners_data.comment: First-time blinkers for a gelding whose mark continues to ease, with his most recent outing at Chepstow potentially compromised by ground softer than ideal — he prefers faster conditions and has that here. Yet to score in recent starts but retains ability over this trip.

runners_data.name: Fancy Dancer
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie fitted for Hayley Burton's low-strike yard; has finished fifth twice in similar company and ran respectably at Sandown over 5f on standard, but the best similar-going stat is just 1W from 15, and this horse's closing game will be fully tested by the congested rear this race shape creates.|
runners_data.comment: First-time tongue-tie for a filly who handles this distance and the fast ground well. She is yet to score in recent starts and has been below her best lately, so must recapture her earlier level to threaten here.

runners_data.name: Southbank
runners_data.note: The key pace-setter for Chris Gordon who holds one win in six runs on similar going over 6f; the decisive tactical advantage here is a solo lead with no challenger — career form shows consistent placings but the ability to fully control tempo on fast Bath ground is the central question.|
runners_data.comment: Back in decent form after a solid effort at Lingfield last time, beaten three and a half lengths off a mark just a pound above this. He handles this distance well and his rating looks fair for his current level, making him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Sisters In The Sky
runners_data.note: Grace Harris pair with Sisters In The Sky in cheekpieces; hit the frame twice in her last five over 6f on good ground and ran a solid third at Goodwood over 6f, so course-related form is live — genuine closer whose finishing effort depends on whether she can extract herself from the redistribution crush.|
runners_data.comment: First-time cheekpieces as a gelding who has previously taken this race at Bath and holds course form, effective over the trip on any going. He tends to be held up and can struggle to get involved at the right time, and has not threatened in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Symbol Of Hope
runners_data.note: Stablemate to Sisters In The Sky, also trained by Grace Harris, making the two entries a factor to note; eight-year-old held up in a group that is already overcrowded at the rear, with a 0 in recent form over 5f at Goodwood the main concern, and pace figures and age both suggest modest expectations.|
runners_data.comment: Goes well at Bath and handles this trip and the quick ground, with his stable having a strong record at this track. He overraced last time when beaten five lengths here, and his form has been inconsistent of late — first-time cheekpieces may help him settle.

runners_data.name: She Went Whoosh
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie and cheekpieces applied for Scott Dixon; sole win in form came over 6f on good at Goodwood and a second there suggests she handles this type of track, but back-to-back 10th and 8th over 7f and 6f are hard to ignore — the headgear combination is the one live flag for a bounce-back here.|
runners_data.comment: First-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces for a filly who failed to see out the trip when well beaten at Brighton last time; she is best on artificial surfaces or with cut in the ground, neither of which applies today. Without a win in over a year, she faces a difficult task here.

races.paceDynamic: Southbank is the lone confirmed front runner in this 5½f Bath handicap on firm ground and should dictate from the outset without any genuine pace pressure, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop throughout. With no other natural leader to push her, she can find her own rhythm down the centre of the track and aim to steal a march on the field from the front. The rest of the eight-runner field is composed almost entirely of hold-up types — Hidden Verse, Fancy Dancer, Sisters In The Sky, Symbol Of Hope, and She Went Whoosh are all genuine closers redistributed into midfield on the map because there is simply no space for them all at the rear in this race shape; of these, Neptune Legend and the better-credentialled hold-up horses are most likely to actually secure their preferred position. A single, uncontested front runner on fast ground at a track where Bath's downhill finish can reward those who travel freely and conserve energy points clearly toward front-running or prominent profiles benefiting here, with late closers facing a stern test against a horse allowed a soft lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Southbank Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Southbank is allowed to stride clear from the gates and sets a measured pace that suits only her.
scenarios.body: If Southbank is allowed to stride clear from the gates and sets a measured pace that suits only her.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Arrive In Time
scenarios.trigger: If Southbank sets an unexpectedly generous gallop and the hold-up horses find a clean, unobstructed run.
scenarios.body: If Southbank sets an unexpectedly generous gallop and the hold-up horses find a clean, unobstructed run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Produces Shock
scenarios.trigger: If the congested midfield and rear group cause interference and a lower-rated stayer threads through late.
scenarios.body: If the congested midfield and rear group cause interference and a lower-rated stayer threads through late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Late
scenarios.trigger: If Southbank gets no cover and the lone-leader exertion on firm ground catches up with her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Southbank gets no cover and the lone-leader exertion on firm ground catches up with her inside the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: Southbank (Luke Morris) — watch whether she is allowed a soft lead from the gates; if no horse challenges her early, this race shape locks in and the probability of Scenario A rises sharply.

Neptune Legend — off just two days since winning, watch the betting market closely for any sign David Egan's booking reflects connections' confidence in the quick turnaround; if supported, this horse's recent form makes him the most dangerous hold-up threat.

Hidden Verse and Fancy Dancer — both genuine closers forced into midfield by the crowded rear; watch the draw and early positioning at the start, as either being shuffled further back than mapped could effectively eliminate their chance in a race where Southbank controls the pace.

Sisters In The Sky and Symbol Of Hope (Grace Harris, same stable) — two runners from one small yard in the same race; watch for any declared stable instructions or jockey tactics that reveal which is the primary runner, as the pair could interfere with each other's runs in the congested closing group.

Firm ground confirmation across all three earlier 5½f races on the card — the going report is consistent throughout the evening, so there is no prospect of softening; horses with firm-ground concerns flagged in similar-going stats should be noted accordingly.

races.name: Lansdown Golf Club Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Havana's Dream
runners_data.note: Ronald Harris runner last out just 4 days ago; wears a hood (hg:p), returns to firm ground where it has placed once in three tries, but its natural rearward style is squeezed into a midfield slot here — finishing position likely to reflect that compromise.
runners_data.comment: Exposed as a poor performer with little worthwhile form to speak of, she races again just four days after her last start; her pedigree is geared towards sprint distances rather than 8f, and first-time cheekpieces offer limited reason for encouragement at the foot of the ratings.

runners_data.name: Knightmare
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave is a major jockey upgrade on an OR-49 horse that has two placed efforts in similar going — a true hold-up type in reality but likely to ride closer than usual given the redistribution; the step back from 10-12f to a flat 1m is a query.
runners_data.comment: Placed in three of his last four starts and second last time with a positive ride, he now wears blinkers; his trainer is in good form and he handles fast ground over 8f, making him the standout pick in this open race.

runners_data.name: Letsbeatsepsis
runners_data.note: Gary & Josh Moore stable are in form (4/20 T14); third and second in recent runs suggests consistent placing form, and a hold-up style suits if the late gallop dries up — 22 days off is manageable.
runners_data.comment: Has twice been placed second in recent starts showing he can compete at this level, but was off the pace when stepped back up in trip at Brighton most recently; an inconsistent sort from a wide draw, he handles sound ground and 8f here should suit better.

runners_data.name: Monks Mead
runners_data.note: The lone pace-setter; Mark Usher yard quiet (0/14 T14) but the horse is the structural pivot of the entire race — has placed twice in its last six, including a runner-up at Wolverhampton; firm ground and an uncontested lead are the key enablers.
runners_data.comment: Back to his best when a close third in a classified race most recently, he is a generally consistent performer over 7-10f on sound ground; he comes here in good heart and ranks among the leading threats in this open field.

runners_data.name: Baynoona
runners_data.note: Sue Gardner has only 2 runs in the 14-day window; wears no headgear; one place finish from 15 runs on comparable ground and is a genuine closer whose chart position overstates how forward it will actually race — a modest each-way chance at best.
runners_data.comment: A previous course-and-distance winner whose recent efforts have slipped below her best, she had no clear excuse when beaten seven lengths at Chepstow last time; handles this distance and going, but needs to recapture earlier levels to make an impact here.

runners_data.name: Blue Hero
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle stable in quiet form but Joe Leavy takes the ride; has placed twice on firm-equivalent going in 15 tries — an eight-year-old who naturally sits well off the pace but the crowded hold-up division means it may end up closer than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Drawn widest of all in this field and well beaten at Bath last time when stepped up in trip, he has a track he likes and handles firm ground; 8f may be on the short side given his best form comes over 10-12f.

runners_data.name: Eye Of The Water
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old with Luke Morris in the saddle; wears a hood (hg:p); consistent fourth-sixth finisher on good-to-firm, rarely wins (no win since records show) but holds its form well enough to sneak a place from a stalking midfield berth.
runners_data.comment: An experienced campaigner who performed to his level when beaten five lengths last time, he tries first-time cheekpieces from a wide draw; the 7/8f trip suits but he goes best with plenty of give, making the firm conditions here less than ideal.

runners_data.name: Hammal
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish — form string 6/7000 is damning, and its last five runs show a deteriorating trajectory; OR 50 is flattering given recent evidence and a hold-up style won't rescue it from its own tendency to stop.
runners_data.comment: Tailed off three times in his last five starts and well beaten down the field at Chepstow most recently, he has plenty to prove at this level; his better form has come at 7f on the all-weather, and the switch to turf over 8f adds further doubt.

runners_data.name: Olivia Jane
runners_data.note: Wears blinkers (hg:b); last six runs read 4000-6 which is very poor, and two recent question-mark results over 16f suggest a horse that has been campaigned ambitiously — dropping back to 1m may help marginally but hard to fancy.
runners_data.comment: Out of form in her last five starts across both codes, she is fitted with blinkers today; beaten eight lengths at Chepstow most recently, she has yet to transfer her better all-weather level to the turf and faces a tough assignment here.

runners_data.name: Scenario
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa is the standout jockey booking in this field for Tony Carroll, who has a strong 10/51 T14 strike rate — the horse won at 1m on good ground in its last five runs and has a rare firm-ground win on record; the form and stable angle make it the most interesting hold-up runner here.
runners_data.comment: A course-and-distance winner who handles the going and represents a handler with a strong record at this venue, she was well held at Chepstow last time; unreliable on her day but with proven form at Bath, she is capable of going close if putting her best foot forward.

runners_data.name: Star Of Atlantis
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle second runner; wears hood (hg:p); all recent starts on Wolverhampton Tapeta (standard), so this firm turf is a genuine unknown — 29 days off and a hold-up profile that is naturally pushed forward by the redistribution creates positional uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Performed to her level when a close fourth in a classified race at Wolverhampton last time, she now tries first-time cheekpieces; effective at 7/8f and handles a sound surface, she needs to build on that effort to make an impact here.

runners_data.name: Addmann
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading finishes; three-year-old carrying 126lbs with a form string of 7880-8 — no wins and no places to speak of; naturally suited to sitting well off the pace but the redistribution pushes it closer, compounding its tendency to weaken late.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at this track most recently with little to show from his last five starts, he tries first-time cheekpieces today; needs a trip beyond 6f so the 8f here at least suits the distance, but he has plenty to prove against these rivals.

runners_data.name: Due Destiny
runners_data.note: Three-year-old on 126lbs; placed at 7f and 6f on good-to-firm but steps up to 1m for the first time on firm turf — the trip extension is a live query; wears headgear (hg:h) and is a hold-up type by nature, though its position on the map overstates its likely proximity to the pace.
runners_data.comment: Prone to not settling and drawn wide, she was beaten over six lengths last time but did see out the trip; wearing a hood for the first time today, she handles good ground but needs to relax far better than she has in the past to factor here.

races.paceDynamic: Monks Mead is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner field and, with no genuine rival to push the pace on firm ground at Bath, is set to dictate terms entirely unopposed from the outset. With a sustainable gallop and no pressure from behind, the race will likely be run at a measured tempo through the first half before Monks Mead attempts to grind rivals down on the long straight, exploiting the firm ground which rewards horses that travel economically. The field is dominated by hold-up types — Knightmare, Blue Hero, Star Of Atlantis, Baynoona, Havana's Dream and several others are genuine closers who are mapped to midfield because there are simply too many hold-up horses for the map to accommodate at the rear — of these, Knightmare and Blue Hero are most likely to secure a forward position given their OR and jockey quality. This race shape — an uncontested single pace-setter on fast ground — heavily favours hold-up horses with a strong finishing kick who can benefit from a well-judged late challenge, provided they can get into a prominent enough position to deliver their run on a track where getting boxed in behind a wall of horses is a real risk.

scenarios.title: Monks Mead Front-Runs Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Monks Mead is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and the chasing pack leaves their run too late on firm ground.
scenarios.body: If Monks Mead is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and the chasing pack leaves their run too late on firm ground.

scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finishers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses are patiently ridden and produce strong late runs down the Bath straight to reel in Monks Mead.
scenarios.body: If the hold-up horses are patiently ridden and produce strong late runs down the Bath straight to reel in Monks Mead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse positioned in the first half of the field tracks Monks Mead and produces a telling challenge from a closer vantage point.
scenarios.body: If a horse positioned in the first half of the field tracks Monks Mead and produces a telling challenge from a closer vantage point.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Monks Mead finds the firm ground and trip beyond them and weakens sharply, triggering a blanket finish among the closers.
scenarios.body: If Monks Mead finds the firm ground and trip beyond them and weakens sharply, triggering a blanket finish among the closers.

watchPoints.text: Monks Mead — if Tyler Heard elects to go on hard from the start and no rival goes with them, the entire race resolves around whether this horse can be caught; watch for the opening splits to determine whether the pace is truly honest or a dawdle.

Scenario — Silvestre De Sousa's positioning in the early stages is critical: if De Sousa allows Scenario to get trapped wide or too far back in a field of 13, the lone front-runner may have too much ground to make up on firm ground.

Knightmare — Pat Cosgrave may be forced to ride more prominently than this horse prefers given the overcrowded hold-up section; if Cosgrave commits forward early, watch whether Knightmare has the tactical speed to sustain that position over 1m.

Hammal and Addmann — both are flagged as horses that fade in the finish; in a field where several hold-up types may be forced wider and closer than natural, these two are the most likely to cause interference or traffic issues in the straight without threatening the result.

Star Of Atlantis — all recent form is on Tapeta at Wolverhampton; if the firm Bath turf produces any unexpected reaction (stumbling, shuffled back) from this hold-up type, it could create a pocket of trouble for horses racing immediately behind it in the first half of the race.

races.name: MJ Church Handicap

runners_data.name: Sant Alessio
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who showed sim-going form (1W1P from 15 runs on good) and whose trainer Joe Tickle has a modest 1/6 in a 14-day window; 17 days since last run is fine, but this horse needs something to close into and the controlled pace is not ideal.|
runners_data.comment: Holds course and distance form on a sound surface but has been well below his best this term, including when ridden too aggressively and beaten clear at Salisbury last time. A revival is needed but the ability is there.

runners_data.name: Thiscouldbefun
runners_data.note: In first-time headgear (p) and trained by J S Moore (1/13 in 14 days), this runner's natural instinct is to settle at the back — held up rather than racing prominently — meaning their midfield map position flatters their actual tactical options here.|
runners_data.comment: First-time cheekpieces for a filly now back down to the mark at which she last struck, and she handles any ground over this sort of trip. However, she had little excuse when well beaten at Salisbury last time and needs to show more.

runners_data.name: Post Rider
runners_data.note: The confirmed race-shaper who sets the tempo; Lewis Edmunds takes over for Oliver Cole's yard (1/9 in 14 days), and Post Rider's best recent form includes a win on good going — stepping into a lead role on firm Bath is a straightforward tactical assignment.|
runners_data.comment: Third at Goodwood on her latest start after a promising comeback run, she is effective at this distance and handles firm ground well. Her mark looks high enough but she is hitting form at the right time and remains a clear danger.

runners_data.name: Nakaaha
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner who finds the trip and going both within profile — a placed run on firm (2/8f/FIR) in the recent past is the standout sim-going tick; David Egan's booking for the Grace Harris yard (2/18 in 14 days) is worth noting, and 8 days between runs is sharp but workable.|
runners_data.comment: First-time hood for a filly who ran below her recent level when beaten six lengths at Newbury eight days ago. Her handicap mark continues to ease and she handles this distance and going, though she needs to do more.

runners_data.name: Swiped
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who most recently won over a mile on good going, showing the form is live; Ralph Beckett's yard runs at 9/60 in 14 days (strong) and Edward Greatrex is a capable handler, but Swiped will need to find a clear run off a potentially slow pace.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap here last time by two and a quarter lengths, benefiting from a drop in class and extra trip, and he is suited by this distance and sound surface. First-time blinkers and he still looks ahead of the assessor.

runners_data.name: Naval Ensign
runners_data.note: Carries a hood and tongue-tie and is a genuine last-off-the-pace type whose true running style places them further back than the map suggests; Nikki Evans sends out just 1/3 runners in the 14-day window and the OR of 59 makes the task harder at this trip on fast ground.|
runners_data.comment: First-time hood and tongue-tie as she attempts to build on her latest run here, where she was fourth after meeting interference when making her challenge. Inconsistent and held up, she faces a stiff task at these weights.

runners_data.name: Ebn Sabt
runners_data.note: Three-year-old running out of a poor recent sequence (1467700) in first-time blinkers, trained by Ben Lund who has drawn a blank in two recent runners (0/2, 14d); a natural hold-up horse displaced into midfield by the field's composition, and the form string does not inspire confidence.|
runners_data.comment: First-time blinkers for a gelding who has been out of form for several starts, most recently finishing down the field at Wolverhampton. He handles this distance on artificial surfaces but is hard to fancy here with his turf figures uninspiring.

races.paceDynamic: Post Rider is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no genuine challenger likely to press them from the gates, they should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over Bath's flat mile on firm ground. Nakaaha is the only other runner with a prominent tag and will likely track Post Rider in second, meaning the pace is unlikely to be truly searching — a measured tempo on fast ground that keeps the race together until the final two furlongs. The field holds more hold-up types than can be genuinely accommodated at the rear: Thiscouldbefun, Ebn Sabt, and Naval Ensign are all true closers who will be shuffled into a midfield cluster rather than finding a clean last-off-the-pace position, which blunts their ability to produce a decisive late run. A controlled single pace-setter on firm ground over a flat mile favours a horse tracking the leader in a prominent position, able to pounce in the straight without needing a strong pace to close into.

watchPoints.text: Post Rider controls the fractions entirely unchallenged — watch whether Lewis Edmunds elects to kick on early in the straight, potentially getting first run on every horse in the field before the closers can respond.

Nakaaha (hg:h, hood) has had only 8 days between runs; watch at the start for any signs of freshness or reluctance to settle, as a tardy break or keenness early would compromise their clean tracking position behind Post Rider.

Swiped has dropped to 3yo minimum weight (130lbs) and arrives on the back of a win — watch whether they are held up wider than ideal or trapped in behind the midfield cluster, as Bath's straight is short and gaps can close quickly on firm ground.

The three redistributed hold-up horses (Thiscouldbefun, Naval Ensign, Ebn Sabt) will all be in the same mid-race zone; watch for traffic trouble entering the final two furlongs if the pace is slow and they all simultaneously attempt to find a run on the outside.

races.name: Magnum Scaffolding Contracts Handicap

runners_data.name: Pivotal Days
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator for Syd Hosie, Ashley Lewis claims 5lb, but recent form (9-8-5-7-0) is deeply uninspiring and all five recent runs have been over longer trips at Goodwood or Sandown — the step back to Bath on firm ground offers no obvious key, and from the back of this field, the uncontested lead pace gives little to close into.
runners_data.comment: Poor form throughout the season in both codes, he was well down the field in a staying event at Ascot most recently; his better juvenile work came over shorter trips with give underfoot, so this 12f on firm offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Charm
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old confirmed front-runner for Georgina Nicholls, whose T14 record of 0/4 is modest; blinkers worn, and recent runs over 1m1f-1m2f at Sandown and Goodwood suggest 1m3½f is a slight stretch, but the uncontested lead on fast ground is a significant structural advantage that overrides most negatives.
runners_data.comment: Below her best when beaten nine lengths at Kempton most recently, she drops to a lower mark than her last win and arrives in first-time blinkers; effective at 12f and handles a sound surface, she needs to find a significant improvement on that effort.

runners_data.name: Offiah's Boy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Joe Tickle (T14: 1/6), Taylor Fisher rides; similar-going form shows a second from 15 runs which is faint but meaningful, and two recent starts at Sandown over a mile show some effort — will likely be closest to Sea Of Charm and benefits most from the controlled gallop without being the one doing the work.
runners_data.comment: Back on a reduced mark after what looked a fitness-restoring spin at Chepstow most recently, he has excelled on fast ground over 8-11f and the distance step to 12f should suit; yet to win in his last five starts, but rated second in this field and conditions favour him.

runners_data.name: Lakota Chief
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for Archie Watson (T14: 3/32 showing the yard in form), Pierre-Louis Jamin takes the ride; all three career runs have been over 7f-8f at Sandown on standard, so 1m3½f on firm is a significant unproven step in trip — holds up by nature but may secure a forward tracking position if others drop out.
runners_data.comment: A big, strong type who has appeared to find a mile on the sharp side, this step up to 12f looks the right assignment; beaten eight lengths in a maiden at Lingfield on his latest outing, he returns from a four-month absence and could prove better over further.

runners_data.name: We Ride At Dawn
runners_data.note: A hold-up type for Robert Edwards (T14: 0/3), Joe Leavy rides; the best piece of form is a second over 1m2f at Goodwood which shows the step up in trip is likely to suit, but the undemanding pace this race will generate makes it structurally awkward for a closer, and a 30-day break adds mild uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up by a length last time on a lower mark, she showed improved form stepping up in trip and her breeding points to middle-distance tests; the 12f here is a positive step and she is capable of further progress, despite being yet to win in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Barak Warrior
runners_data.note: James Keane sends out this three-year-old (T14: 1/1, 100%), Silvestre De Sousa a significant booking; naturally races from the back but all three runs have been over 1m-1m2f on soft or good — firm ground at a longer trip is untested, and with the race unlikely to truly set up for late runners, De Sousa's quality may not be enough to overcome the shape.
runners_data.comment: Expected to improve for the switch into handicap company over this longer trip, he was held up in his novice races and is the type likely to stay further than 10f; well beaten most recently but handicapping for the first time, the conditions are more straightforward and he is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Campeona
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's three-year-old returns after 186 days off, Luke Morris rides; all three starts have been over 7f-8f at Sandown on standard, so both the trip extension and the firm ground are unknown quantities — a natural closer who will need a much stronger pace than Sea Of Charm is likely to supply, and the long layoff adds significant doubt.
runners_data.comment: Middle-distance bred and likely to relish a genuine stamina test, she failed to see out the trip when ridden prominently at a longer distance in a novice at Wolverhampton most recently; moderate in three starts so far and returning after a six-month absence, yet to win, but the 12f could bring out more.

races.paceDynamic: Sea Of Charm is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will stride out uncontested from the gates over 1m3½f on firm ground at Bath. That uncontested lead on a flat, fast track creates a genuinely sustainable, even gallop — Sea Of Charm can control every fraction without burning fuel, making it very difficult for hold-up horses to generate the momentum they need from the rear. The field behind is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up and late-running types — We Ride At Dawn, Pivotal Days, Lakota Chief, Barak Warrior and Campeona are all natural closers — but the compressed, undemanding pace risks leaving them with no real race to run into. This race shape strongly favours the prominent or controlled-pace profile: a horse who can track Sea Of Charm at close range and kick off a steady gallop, rather than a pure hold-up type relying on a strong pace to close into. Lakota Chief, Barak Warrior and Campeona are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because there are simply too many closers for them all to operate from their natural position — of those, Lakota Chief (Jamin aboard for Watson) is most likely to actually secure a forward tracking berth, with Barak Warrior the next most likely.

watchPoints.text: Sea Of Charm's energy management is the fulcrum of this race — if William Cox misjudges the pace and goes too slow, the entire field bunches and the front-runner's structural advantage evaporates instantly.

Campeona's 186-day absence for Sir Mark Prescott is notable — Prescott horses returning from long breaks can be fit first time up, but the unknown fitness combined with an unproven trip and going makes this runner a genuine wildcard in the finish.

Lakota Chief has only raced three times, all over 7f-8f, and Pierre-Louis Jamin will need to decide very quickly whether to push forward or settle — if the field concedes the lead tamely and the pace is falsely slow, Jamin's tactical decision in the first furlong could define the race shape.

De Sousa's booking for Barak Warrior (James Keane, T14: 1/1) flags stable confidence, but the horse's natural style is compromised by the uncontested pace — watch how far off the leader De Sousa elects to settle, as that gap will indicate whether the stable expects a pace collapse or a genuine gallop.

The firm going is consistent across the entire Bath card and has held all evening — no deterioration risk, but any horse with a going preference for a sounder surface should be fully advantaged, and Sea Of Charm's record on similar ground is the key qualifying angle to check before the off.
